high3.name: High-3 (Legacy)
high3.eligibleDates: Entered service between September 8, 1980 and December 31, 2017
high3.baseFormula: Years of Service × 2.5% × Average of Highest 36 Months Base Pay
high3.taxStatus: Subject to federal and state income tax (some states exempt)
high3.notes: Most common system for active duty retirees. Uses average of highest 36 months of base pay.

brs.name: BRS (Blended Retirement System)
brs.eligibleDates: Entered service on or after January 1, 2018 (or opted in before Dec 31, 2018)
brs.baseFormula: Years of Service × 2.0% × Average of Highest 36 Months Base Pay

continuationPay.description: Lump sum bonus at 12 years of service

examples.description: 20 years × 2.0% = 40% of high-3 average (but TSP offsets lower pension)

brs.taxStatus: Subject to federal and state income tax (some states exempt)
brs.notes: Lower pension than High-3, but TSP matching makes up difference. Better for those who separate before 20 years.

redux.name: REDUX
redux.eligibleDates: Entered service between August 1, 1986 and December 31, 2017 AND accepted Career Status Bonus

csb.description: $30,000 lump sum in exchange for reduced retirement

redux.baseFormula: Years of Service × 2.5% × Average of Highest 36 Months Base Pay (with penalty)
redux.age62Adjustment: One-time catch-up adjustment to match High-3, then normal COLA resumes

examples.description: 20 years = 40% (10% penalty). Receives $30K CSB at year 15.
examples.note: At age 62, adjusts to match what High-3 would have been

redux.taxStatus: Subject to federal and state income tax (some states exempt)
redux.notes: Very few people chose this. Penalty at retirement, reduced COLA, but $30K upfront. Not recommended.

finalPay.name: Final Pay
finalPay.baseFormula: Years of Service × 2.5% × Final Month Base Pay

examples.description: Uses last month's base pay instead of 36-month average

finalPay.taxStatus: Subject to federal and state income tax (some states exempt)
finalPay.notes: Grandfathered system. Very few active retirees under this system. Uses final month instead of high-36 average.

generalNotes.taxStatus: All military retirement pay is subject to federal income tax. Some states exempt military retirement (AL, AK, FL, HI, IL, KS, LA, MS, NV, NH, PA, SD, TN, TX, WA, WY).
generalNotes.vaDisability: You can receive both military retirement AND VA disability, but there may be an offset depending on your situation.
generalNotes.socialSecurity: Military retirement does not reduce Social Security benefits. You can receive both.
generalNotes.survivors: Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) available for 6.5% of gross retirement pay.
generalNotes.colaAdjustments: COLA adjustments happen annually in December, based on CPI-U.
generalNotes.high36Calculation: High-36 average = sum of highest 36 months of base pay ÷ 36. Does NOT include BAH, BAS, or special pays.

partialExemptionStates.Colorado: Up to age 65: $20,000 exempt. Over 65: $24,000 exempt
